problem:
The velocity, in $\text{m/s}$, of a subatomic particle is modeled using the function $v(t)=2{csc}^{2}⁡(t)$ for $\pi <t<2\pi .$

Earlier part 1:

Find the velocity of the particle at $t=\frac{7\pi }{6}.$

                                        $\text{m/s}$

Earlier part 2:

${lim}_{t\to 2{\pi }^{-}}v(t)\,=\,$

                            
                                    
                            
                                        $\infty$

Earlier part 3:

The acceleration $a(t)$ of the particle is given by the derivative of the velocity with respect to time. Find the function $a(t).$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $a(t)=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        $-4\csc(t)^2$                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $\cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡t$

Earlier part 4:

$\int v(t)\,\text{d}t\,\,=\,$

                                         $+\text{ }C$

Earlier part 5:

Another particle has a velocity function given by ${v}_{2}(t)=t\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2}).$ Evaluate the velocity of this particle at $t=\frac{16\pi }{3}.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${v}_{2}(\frac{16\pi }{3})\,=\,$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        $-\frac{8\pi}{3}$                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $\text{m/s}$

Earlier part 6:

Find ${lim}_{t\to 5\pi /2}{v}_{2}(t)\,=\,$

                            
                                    
                            
                                        $-\frac{5\pi\sqrt{2}}{4}$

Current part:

Find the acceleration function ${a}_{2}(t)$ of the second particle.

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${a}_{2}(t)\,=\,$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}

feedback.worked_solution:
Substituting $t=\frac{5\pi }{2}$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 5\pi /2}{v}_{2}(t) & ={lim}_{t\to 5\pi /2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{5\pi }{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{2}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{5\sqrt{2}\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
